findings.name: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption (Homestead)
findings.description: A veteran of the U.S. Armed Forces who is permanently and totally disabled as a result of a service-connected disability, and who files a certificate signed by the county service officer certifying the disability, is exempt from property tax on their dwelling house and the land on which it sits, up to five acres. Qualified surviving spouses (unremarried, residing in and owning the house) may claim the same exemption. A 2024 law (Act 116, formerly Bill 3116) lets a veteran or surviving spouse claim the exemption immediately for the entire year in which the disability occurs, rather than waiting until the following tax year, and applies to tax years beginning after 2023. Separately, a bill (H.4700) that would let veterans with a partial (less than total) service-connected disability rating claim a proportional exemption equal to their disability percentage was still only 'introduced' and pending in the House as of this session's check (January 2026) — it is NOT yet law, so this file does not treat partial-rating exemptions as available. The statute itself does not state a specific percentage threshold beyond 'permanently and totally disabled.'
findings.value: Full exemption from property tax on primary residence and up to 5 acres
otherReqs: Service-connected disability certified as permanent and total
Certificate signed by county service officer filed with SC Dept. of Revenue
Qualified surviving spouses (unremarried, residing in and owning the home) may also claim
documentation: County service officer certification of permanent and total service-connected disability
findings.sourceExcerpt: a veteran of the Armed Forces of the United States who is permanently and totally disabled as a result of a service-connected disability... A qualified surviving spouse... remains unmarried, resides in the house, and owns it in fee or for life.

findings.name: South Carolina State Veterans Homes
findings.description: South Carolina operates six State Veterans Homes offering skilled or intermediate nursing home care: E. Roy Stone Veterans Pavilion (Columbia), Veterans' Victory House (Walterboro), Richard Michael Campbell Veterans Home (Anderson), Veteran Village (Florence), Palmetto Patriots Home (Gaffney), and Patriot's Village (Sumter). Admission is limited to veterans separated under general or honorable conditions who qualify as South Carolina citizens and are in need of skilled or intermediate nursing home care.
findings.value: Skilled or intermediate nursing home care at state veterans homes
otherReqs: Separated from U.S. Armed Forces under general or honorable conditions
South Carolina residency
Meets medical admission criteria for skilled or intermediate nursing care
findings.agency: South Carolina Department of Veterans' Affairs
documentation: DD-214 or other proof of discharge status
findings.sourceExcerpt: Veterans who have been separated from the U.S. Armed Forces under general or honorable conditions and qualify as South Carolina citizens who are in need of skilled or intermediate nursing home care.

findings.name: Free Tuition Program for Children of Certain War Veterans
findings.description: Under S.C. Code §59-111-20, children age 26 or younger of a wartime veteran may attend any South Carolina state-supported college, university, or technical college tuition-free if the veteran was killed in action, died from other causes while in service, died of disease or disability resulting from service, was a prisoner of war, is permanently and totally disabled as determined by the VA from any cause, was awarded the Congressional Medal of Honor, is missing in action, or was awarded the Purple Heart for combat wounds. Both the student and the veteran (if living) generally must have established South Carolina residency for at least the 12 continuous months before application, though a later amendment also allows a child who has been a South Carolina resident since birth to qualify regardless of the veteran's current residence. The waiver covers tuition only, not fees, room, board, or books.
findings.value: Free tuition at SC state-supported colleges, universities, and technical colleges
otherReqs: Child of qualifying veteran, age 26 or under
Veteran served during an officially recognized war period
Qualifies via any of several disjunctive paths (KIA, died of service-connected causes, POW, permanently/totally disabled, Medal of Honor, MIA, or Purple Heart) — not solely a disability-rating gate
Residency requirements for student and/or veteran
Covers tuition only, not fees/room/board/books
findings.agency: South Carolina Department of Veterans' Affairs, Education Office
documentation: VA determination of permanent and total disability (or other qualifying veteran status documentation)

findings.name: State Employment Veteran's Preference
findings.description: Effective January 1, 2021, honorably discharged members of the U.S. Armed Forces who are given employment preference by the federal government receive preference for appointment and employment in every South Carolina state government agency and higher education institution. Hiring agencies and institutions must interview at least one qualified veteran applicant for every full-time-equivalent position posted, unless no veteran applicant meets the position's training and experience requirements. Applicants must submit a DD-214 with their state employment application; those claiming veteran status without a DD-214 do not receive preference.
findings.value: Hiring preference and guaranteed-interview requirement for state government and higher-education jobs
otherReqs: Honorable discharge with federal employment preference eligibility
Must meet the position's minimum training/experience requirements
DD-214 must accompany the state employment application
documentation: DD-214 / Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty
findings.sourceExcerpt: effective January 1, 2021... honorably discharged members of the United States Armed Forces who are given employment preference by the United States Government will be given preference for appointment and employment in every state government agency and higher education institution... findings.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate (Fee-Waived)
findings.description: South Carolina's SCDMV issues a Disabled Veteran license plate at no registration fee to veterans discharged honorably or under general-under-honorable-conditions who provide a letter from the county or U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs office documenting the loss of, or loss of use of, a leg, arm, or vision, or a total-and-permanent service-connected disability rating. This standard Disabled Veteran plate does not carry handicap-parking privileges. A separate 'Disabled Veteran (wheelchair)' plate is also free, includes free metered/timed parking and handicap-parking privileges, and additionally requires Form RG-007A signed by a licensed physician. Applications (Form MV-37) must be mailed to SCDMV Headquarters; plates are not issued in person or online. A registrant may hold up to three military-related plates.
findings.value: License plate registration fee waived for qualifying disabled veterans
otherReqs: Discharge status of honorable or general under honorable conditions
Letter from county or VA office documenting qualifying disability
Wheelchair variant additionally requires Form RG-007A signed by a physician
Registration by mail only to SCDMV Headquarters

findings.name: Property Tax Exemption on Two Vehicles for Disabled Veterans
findings.description: Under S.C. Code §12-37-220(B)(3), a veteran who is permanently and totally disabled as a result of a service-connected disability is exempt from property tax on up to two private passenger vehicles owned or leased by the veteran; the exemption also extends to a vehicle titled to the veteran's spouse if the spouse resides with the veteran. This is a property-tax exemption administered via the county auditor/treasurer and SC Department of Revenue (Form PT-401I), distinct from the SCDMV's separate no-fee Disabled Veteran license plate. This session could not confirm, on an official source, any additional waiver of the SCDMV's biennial vehicle registration/renewal fee itself beyond the free Disabled Veteran plate documented in the license_plate entry — that specific claim is not made here.
findings.value: Exemption from property tax on up to two private passenger vehicles
otherReqs: Service-connected disability certified as permanent and total
Applies to up to two vehicles owned or leased by the veteran (or the veteran's co-resident spouse)
Form PT-401I filed with SC Department of Revenue after DMV registration
documentation: County service officer certification of permanent and total service-connected disability
findings.sourceExcerpt: two private passenger vehicles owned or leased by any disabled veteran... qualify for exemption if the veteran has special license tags or a certificate of total and permanent disability filed with the Department of Motor Vehicles.

findings.name: Disability Hunting and Fishing License
findings.description: South Carolina residents of at least 365 days who are certified disabled and receiving disability benefits from a qualifying program (including the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs) are entitled to a free statewide hunting and fishing license through the SC Department of Natural Resources. This Disability License is valid for 3 years from the date of issue, and disability recertification is required to renew — it is not a lifetime license by default. Veterans who are paraplegic, quadriplegic, or legally blind and provide a doctor's statement are instead issued a Lifetime Disability License.
findings.value: Free 3-year disability hunting/fishing license (or a Lifetime Disability License for paraplegic, quadriplegic, or legally blind applicants)
otherReqs: South Carolina resident for at least 365 days
Current (within 12 months) disability certification from a qualifying program, including VA disability benefits
Recertification required every 3 years unless issued a Lifetime Disability License for paraplegia, quadriplegia, or legal blindness
findings.agency: South Carolina Department of Natural Resources
documentation: Current disability certification from VA (or other qualifying program) dated within the past 12 months
Doctor's statement for the Lifetime Disability License variant
findings.sourceExcerpt: If you have been a resident of SC for at least 365 days and have been declared disabled and are receiving disability benefits from one of the following agencies you are entitled to a free disability hunting and fishing license... A Disability License is valid for 3 years from date of issue... If you are paraplegic, quadriplegic, or legally blind and include a statement from your doctor you will be issued a Lifetime Disability License.

findings.name: Military Retirement Pay State Income Tax Exemption
findings.description: South Carolina fully exempts military retirement pay from state income tax, with no age requirement and no earned-income cap, for tax years after 2021. Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP), Reserve Component SBP (RCSBP), and Retired Serviceman's Family Protection Plan (RSFPP) payments are also fully exempt. This benefit applies to all retired servicemembers regardless of VA disability rating and is separate from VA disability compensation, which is already untaxed at the federal and state level.
findings.value: 100% exemption of military retirement pay (and SBP/RCSBP/RSFPP payments) from SC state income tax
otherReqs: Applies to military retirement pay for tax years after 2021
No age or income cap
documentation: 1099-R or other proof of military retirement pay
findings.sourceExcerpt: military retiree pay 100-percent exempt from state income tax with no earned-income cap... Workforce Enhancement and Military Recognition Act
